entities.name: Thornback boar

fields.does: A boar the size of a hay cart, with bristles thick and sharp as bramble. It charges anything that smells of food.
fields.limits: It can't turn quickly. Step aside and it hits the nearest tree.
fields.story: Thornbacks are one of the beasts the Blight is pushing out of the deep woods. GuildScribe's bounty on them is new, and so is its bestiary page.

entities.name: Gloamowl

fields.does: A grey owl as big as a dog that hunts at dusk. It's one of the wood's very few true flyers.
fields.limits: It's nearly blind by daylight and stays in its roost.
fields.story: Hunters say if you hear one, it's already behind you.

entities.name: Barrowbear

fields.does: A moss-backed bear that digs its den into old earthworks along the road and treats the road as its own.
fields.limits: It sleeps through most of winter, and it won't leave its den's sight for long.
fields.story: Merchants pay their escorts double for the stretch past a barrowbear's den.

entities.name: Goblin raiders

fields.story: The ones that reach the croplands raid Stoutwell's crops. The ones adventurers meet are the ones that didn't get that far.

entities.name: Driftmaw

fields.does: A floating gasbag the size of a cart, drifting just above the canopy and trailing sticky tendrils that haul prey up into its mouth.
fields.limits: Its movement is dictated by prevailing winds; a strong gust can easily carry it away.
fields.story: Floating monsters like it are the reason Stoutwell's walls need human archers. The westward migration of these creatures is attributed to the expansion of the Blight’s influence.

entities.name: Hollowstag

fields.does: A stag nearly fifteen feet tall at the antlers. Its antlers are hollow and whistle as it runs, which is how hunters hear it coming.
fields.limits: Too tall for thick woods, it keeps to clearings and old roads.
fields.story: This towering creature necessitates Stoutwell’s reliance on ranged weaponry for defense. A hollowstag antler would be the first proof of the deep woods' beasts ever brought to GuildScribe.

entities.name: Rootwyrm

fields.does: A serpent as thick as a mill wheel that lives in the tangle of roots under the deep woods, surfacing to swallow whatever stands still.
fields.limits: It needs soft, living soil to move through. The Blight's dry, grey ground is driving it out.
fields.story: The Blight killing the roots is what brought rootwyrms to the surface.

entities.name: The Mosswarden

fields.does: A beast so old a small forest grows on its back. It walks so slowly that most people who see it think it's a hill.
fields.limits: It almost never runs, and it stops to root itself every season.
fields.story: It has wandered the deep woods since Stoutwell was founded. If the Blight has driven even the Mosswarden out, things are worse in there than anyone knows. Murrow might remember it.

entities.name: Rootwraiths
entities.body:
_From a lore-keeper chat, 2026-11-08 · Physics & nature._

Name: Rootwraiths
Kind: Plant/Spirit (Entanglement)
The Rule: These animated root constructs attempt to ensnare creatures within their grasping tendrils.
How It Works: They move slowly, relying on surprise attacks and attempting to grapple targets using thorny vines. Success requires a successful Dexterity saving throw against their reach and bludgeoning damage.
Costs and Limits: Vulnerable to fire damage, requiring significant effort to destroy.  Detection requires a high Perception roll.
Who It Affects: Primarily melee fighters, archers struggling to maintain aim under pressure.
What It Changes: Introduces a constant threat of being restrained and slowed down by spectral vegetation.
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (Suggested) – Can they be reasoned with or manipulated?

entities.name: Gloomshrooms
entities.body:
Name: Gloomshrooms
Kind: Fungus/Psychic (Hallucination)
The Rule: These clusters release spores that induce vivid nightmares and disorientation in those nearby.
How It Works: The spores require a DC12 Wisdom save to resist; failure results in temporary madness - confusion, paranoia, and reduced actions for one round. Bright light rapidly disperses the spores.
Costs and Limits: Requires proximity to avoid. Vulnerability to bright light. Limited range. 
Who It Affects: Individuals susceptible to fear or anxiety are more vulnerable. Those with low wisdom scores take a higher penalty. 
What It Changes: Alters perception, reduces combat effectiveness, creates opportunities for manipulation.
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (suggested) – How long do effects last? Do certain herbs provide resistance?

entities.name: Stonegrubs
entities.body:
Name: Stonegrubs
Kind: Earth/Animal (Burrowing Assault)
The Rule: These armored grubs use their burrowing abilities to ambush targets from beneath the ground.
How it works: They move quickly through loose earth and stone, attempting to grapple prey with powerful jaws. Attacks involve Dexterity saving throws against piercing damage and potentially stunning targets.
Costs & Limits: Slow movement on hard surfaces. Effectiveness depends heavily on terrain – requires soft soil.  Vulnerable to blunt attacks. 
Who It Affects: Primarily melee fighters caught off-guard, those moving through wooded areas.
What It Changes: Introduces an element of surprise and vulnerability during travel or battle.
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (Suggested) - Can they be lured into traps?

entities.name: Shadowhawks
entities.body:
Name: Shadowhawks
Kind: Animal/Darkness (Silent Predation)
The Rule: These evolved hawks utilize darkness and silent flight to harass and incapacitate prey. 
How It Works: Benefit from low light conditions; have advantage on stealth checks in shadows. Their attack relies on a single hit, but follow up attacks can easily overwhelm a target with overwhelming speed. 
Costs & Limits: Vulnerable to bright light and fire. Requires careful tracking and positioning. 
Who It Affects: Archers, scouts, any vulnerable creature exposed without cover. 
What It Changes: Adds a new aerial threat to the Deep Woods. 
Clashes With Canon: None
Open Questions: (suggested) – Do they leave behind traces after their strikes?

entities.name: Silken Stalker
entities.body:
_Made up by the AI in rest mode, 2026-11-07 · about a creature of the Monster Wood: where it lives, what it does, its limits._

- **Label:** A creature adapted to the damp, echoing depths of the Monster Wood, it communicates through subtle shifts in air pressure and uses this ability for both hunting and defense.
- **What it is:** A "Silken Stalker," a small, serpentine predator about the size of a large dog – roughly three feet long - covered in moss-like fur that blends perfectly with the Monster Wood’s undergrowth. It possesses delicate, membranous wings allowing short bursts of gliding flight.
- **Who:** Native to the deepest sections of the Monster Wood, primarily dwelling amongst ancient, decaying trees near areas saturated with moisture and shadow. They are solitary creatures, rarely interacting with each other or venturing far from their chosen territories.
- **Where:** Specifically found within pockets of the Monster Wood characterized by unusually high humidity—particularly around fallen logs, stagnant pools, and deep ravines where the sunlight struggles to penetrate. Their dens are typically constructed within hollowed-out tree roots or beneath dense tangles of vines.
- **How it Works:** The Silken Stalker doesn't rely on sight or sound; instead, it detects its prey (small animals, birds, even unwary travelers) using specialized organs located along its flanks that sense minute changes in air pressure caused by movement. These ‘pressure whispers’ allow it to pinpoint targets with incredible accuracy, effectively creating a 3D “map” of its surroundings.  It can also use this ability defensively, releasing a concentrated burst of compressed air as a disorienting shockwave.
- **Limits:** Its sensitivity is heavily affected by strong winds or turbulent airflow – making open spaces perilous. Magical interference, especially spells that create sonic vibrations, severely disrupts its sensory system, causing intense pain and disorientation. Prolonged exposure to fire causes its fur to burn rapidly, stripping away its camouflage and leaving it vulnerable. It cannot reliably track magic users - they simply appear as static noise.
- **Ties:** Murrow has been observing the Silken Stalkers during his research

entities.name: Whisperwind’s Vigil
entities.body:
_Made up by the AI in auto mode, 2026-11-08 · about a creature of the Monster Wood: where it lives, what it does, its limits._

- **What it is:** A spectral hound, native only to the immediate area around the Monster Wood and especially active near Rook’s Watch, that acts as a living early warning system for intruders or significant magical disturbances within a roughly half-mile radius. It doesn't attack, instead emitting mournful howls when something triggers its heightened state – often before any physical threat materializes.
- **Who:** Primarily controlled by Whisperwind, the village’s appointed “Watcher” - essentially a conduit and amplifier for the Hound’s abilities, though not its creator. The Hound itself seems ancient and unbound by normal rules of life and death.
- **Where:** Specifically located along the western edge of Stoutwell where the Monster Wood begins, particularly concentrated around Rook’s Watch, a small elevated platform built atop a naturally occurring rock formation overlooking the woods. Its range extends approximately ½ mile outwards from Rook’s Watch. The wood grows dense enough here that most inhabitants don’t venture this far without Guard escort.
- **How it works:** The Hound appears to be drawn to strong magical signatures—even faint ones—and areas with unusual energy fluctuations. When triggered, it emits three distinct types of howling: a low rumble signifying general unease; a high-pitched whine indicating immediate danger; and a sustained, sorrowful wail if the disturbance is unnatural (like magic gone wrong). Whisperwind can subtly adjust the Hound’s sensitivity, but only through focused meditation and quiet intention.  It requires constant attention, as extended periods of silence or distraction weaken its connection. A significant drain on mana is required for Whisperwind to sustain the contact – roughly equivalent to one hour of focused spellcasting.
- **Limits:** The Hound's effectiveness is directly tied to Whisperwind’s ability to maintain focus. Loud noises, distractions, or emotional distress severely disrupt the link. It cannot “see” in the conventional sense, relying solely on sensory input filtered by its spectral awareness. Additionally, the Hound *cannot* predict the outcome of events – merely alert to their presence. Finally, prolonged exposure to the hound causes a dulling effect - those who stand near it for too long find themselves unusually sluggish and unable

entities.name: Whisperwind’s Vigil
entities.body:
_Made up by the AI in auto mode, 2026-11-08 · about a creature of the Monster Wood: where it lives, what it does, its limits._

- **What it is:** Within the deepest reaches of the Monster Wood, near where the gnarled trees weep sap that glows with an unsettling green light, dwells a creature known only as Rook – a “Rootwraith,” a being formed entirely of intertwined tree roots animated by residual magic left behind by the blight. It doesn't actively hunt or attack, instead meticulously collecting dropped items - lost tools, broken weapons, scraps of clothing – arranging them in intricate patterns around specific, ancient oaks.
- **Who:** Rook is not sentient in any traditional sense. It is a construct, a lingering echo of the blighted wood’s desperate attempt to defend itself, now driven purely by instinctual compulsion. It seems to be roughly humanoid in shape, standing about seven feet tall, its body composed of dark, twisted branches interwoven with glowing moss and thorny vines. The glow isn’t warm, more like sickly moonlight.
- **Where:** Rook resides exclusively within a small clearing approximately five miles into the Monster Wood, marked by three particularly grotesque, weeping oak trees clustered together—these are the focal points for its collection efforts.  The area is perpetually shrouded in mist and choked with fungal growth; a rare pocket untouched by the Blight’s outer reach. Specifically, this clearing sits at the foot of the Brackwood Fringe, where the woods begin to feel truly alien.
- **How it works:** The Rootwraith’s movement is slow but relentless, powered by a subtle manipulation of the surrounding root systems. It can move silently through dense undergrowth, almost as if becoming part of the forest itself. Its primary “attack” mechanism involves ensnaring victims using rapidly extending roots – these aren't aggressive; they simply bind and restrain until the person becomes too exhausted to free themselves. Importantly, it doesn't seem to actively *consume* anything beyond what it collects, instead meticulously arranging them - items collected appear to create a complex map that shifts frequently.  It has no apparent weaknesses other than intense heat or fire--which seems to slowly burn away its form, though quickly re-forms.
- **Limits:** The Rootwraith's influence weakens significantly outside of the immediate
